notes.title: Breathing Life into the Mundane
notes.notes:
[p]Survivors,[/p][p]It’s been a minute since we’ve talked about what’s been in development, hasn’t it? [/p][p]With our heads buried deep in development, we only just realized we have a whole new demo ready for Gamescom, yet we have kept you in the dark about what we’ve been working on![/p][p]We’ll go over the major gameplay features that are new to the Gamescom demo soon, but today, let’s talk about something core to God Save Birmingham: bringing realness to the survival.[/p][p][/p][p]By now, you probably know our goal is to make a medieval zombie survival game grounded in realistic physics. Sure, “medieval” and “zombie” grab attention–but it’s “realistic” that’s the real beast. [/p][p]Why? Because realism is expensive. Like, REALLY expensive. [/p][p]It takes us a lot of time and resources to bring even the most mundane parts of survival to life–making them feel grounded, tactile, and true to real-world physics.[/p][p][/p][p]Let’s take the simple action of eating an apple. Imagine a small red apple just inches away from the character’s face–about to bite in, ready to restore hunger and thirst. That apple can’t look like it’s popped out of thin air and is magically levitating like some cursed fruit, it has to sit perfectly in the hand to feel real and just right.[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45151109/6cbe55854a6b55c79d67e6224d8e58022f4bae12.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Now, imagine doing that not just for an apple, but for cheese, potato, pork, ham, parsnips… You get the idea. [/p][p]Tedious? You bet. [/p][p]Necessary? Absolutely.[/p][p][/p][p]And that's just one type of interaction. There’s literally a whole world of character-object behaviors like picking things up, throwing them, dropping them, swinging them--all of which have to account for context. You wouldn’t swing an apple like you’d swing an axe, would you? [/p][p]We’re deep in the thick of working all this out right now. It feels like we’ve been working on this for years, but really, it’s only been a few months--and there’s still a long way to go. The sheer number of items and interactions tied to them make for long, slow, retina-burning workdays.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45151109/9ccb6a2a27caf3b615ec10d3b0f06a88fe85cc9e.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]And we’re constantly tweaking and refining our animation as we go, of course. Can you spot the subtle difference in our farmer’s throwing motion from a few months ago and what’s currently in the game? [/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45151109/fef61a8c034a1170d447b04938e68aef9254738e.gif"][/img][/p][p] Hopefully, all the tedious work will pay off by the time we launch into Early Access so that this kind of realism becomes invisible--the kind you don’t consciously notice but feel when it’s done right. Until then, you’ll likely run into some glaring collision and animation issues when we run demos and beta tests. But please know that we are working on them, one object at a time![/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45151109/0df3fb66697bb66f7bccac74e24287e0c801d26a.png"][/img][/p][p]Speaking of throwing, falling objects are part of real physics so we’ve been working on that too. And yes, that means we’re working on how an object falls, one individual item at a time. [/p][p]They look pretty cool when they’re all together raining down from the sky like this though, right?[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45151109/03acf52165ef48fed482a97cc0e5cacf21b2fbf8.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Of course, making God Save Birmingham feel more realistic also means making it more faithful to the real 14th century town. That involves a lot of research and we’ve touched on this a bit before in [u][url="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/3073940/view/547852302920188166"]this[/url][/u] blog. The research is never-ending, and in fact, the wealth of information available on Birmingham is the reason we chose it as our setting. Along the way, we’ve been picking up some nuggets of history to reflect in-game.
[/p][p]For example, if you watch our very first trailer, you can see that the St. Martin’s church’s doors are left open [b]outward[/b]. [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45151109/736376615f2c16e02840e06bf6de64433b914909.png"][/img][/p][p]We’ve since then learned that medieval doors in Europe usually opened [b]inward[/b] for security purposes. Isn’t that interesting? After this revelation, we updated the game so doors do just that--open [b]inward[/b]. No more sticking out your entire body to close an open door, risking running into a zombie. It’s like the medieval folks were expecting a zombie apocalypse or something. ːsteammockingː[/p][p][/p][p]Well, hopefully this gives you a little peek into what we’ve been up to. It’s still only a snippet of what we’re working on so come back for the next log![/p][p][/p][p]-ODS Team[/p][p]

[/p]

notes.title: The Role of Physics in God Save Birmingham
notes.notes:
Dear Survivors,

We are so excited to talk to you today about something that is a huge part of our game: physics mechanics. 

Physics-based mechanics have always been an integral part of [i]God Save Birmingham[/i] from the very beginning. It was important to us that it be a key component of the gameplay experience and the sense of immersion. The realistic interactions between characters -- whether they’re human or zombie -- and the environment are what makes our game feel engaging and dynamic.

[h3]Physics-Driven Gameplay Mechanics[/h3]

It’s always been one of our highest priorities to make physics actively shape your gameplay. You can interact with practically every object you encounter, whether it’s lifting, pushing, or throwing. Even your inventory is a factor, hindering your movement when encumbered or aiding your speed when empty. No detail has been overlooked on our quest for depth and realism. 

Explore the world and use your imagination; you’ll be astounded by the freedom of what you can do. Need to clear a path? Move obstacles out of the way! Need to block zombies? Stack furniture to barricade a door! Want to reach a high ledge? Use a table or chair to climb up! Players and zombies can even trip over objects around the world, so watch your step!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45151109/abb5071cbd1b98173e0fac5a207917443c2f4334.gif[/img]

[h3]Challenges in Implementing Physics[/h3]

Integrating an advanced physics system hasn’t been without its challenges, though. While game engines have come a long way towards supporting physics, developing a seamless and bug-free system has still been demanding.

Ensuring every object has accurate collision shapes, weight, density, and friction values is a meticulous process. Unlike typical static world design, where small overlaps or floating objects might go unnoticed, [i]God Save Birmingham[/i] requires precise physical placement, increasing the workload for our designers. To streamline this, we’ve developed specialized tools that help make this process more efficient. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45151109/b4f01774f57a248ec71ac6e93ea71ad2f8dce977.jpg[/img]
[h3]Inspirations from Other Games[/h3]

Playing immersive sims like [i]Half-Life[/i], [i]Portal[/i], and [i]Dishonored[/i] -- pioneers in physics engines -- was a huge inspiration for me to include physics in GSB. I have fond memories of being able to freely pick up, push, and throw anything in the game world. In particular, the Magnesis skill and Ultrahand mechanics in [i]The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild[/i] and [i]Tears of the Kingdom[/i] were incredibly impressive with their intuitive object manipulation and how they contributed to the gameplay.

We’re developing [i]God Save Birmingham[/i] hoping to incorporate that same level of physical freedom, but now in a zombie survival game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45151109/d06a7fca168bbd8942ac2ce52cb7f6404feb9030.jpg[/img]
[h3]Future Enhancements[/h3]

One of the features we’re most excited about integrating is a weather mechanic. Imagine all the possibilities! Fog, rain, a little sunshine (you know, your typical Birmingham weather) — all of it creating new challenges or offering new opportunities. Rain might make surfaces slippery, impacting movement. Lightweight objects might be pushed about by strong wind. 

As we continue working on GSB, it’s our goal to implement physics, along with other environmental and survival simulation elements, as fully as possible into the game’s systems. If you have any ideas, feel free to share them with us!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45151109/55ce598fee10d4beaf0a4a787595ad3687479a5d.gif[/img]

We can’t wait to see how players use these systems creatively, and we look forward to sharing more as we continue improving the game.

Hyeonseong Cha, Creative Director

notes.title: Bringing 14th-Century Birmingham to Life
notes.notes:
Welcome back, Survivors!

In our previous [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/3073940/announcements/detail/547851035326021922]dev log[/url], we talked a little bit about why we chose Birmingham, England, as the setting for [i]God Save Birmingham[/i]. Our goal has always been to create a medieval world that feels as authentic as possible, and through extensive research, we found that 14th-century Birmingham was the perfect backdrop for our survival game.

The 1300s were a historical time, shaped by the Black Death, and Birmingham at the time was a growing market town. We’ve spent time digging into historical records, old maps, and academic sources to understand how people lived, what they ate, and how the city was structured. We even found a model of medieval Birmingham to help visualize the layout!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45151109/7faa80883eb1bb0606381c3f59a058763896092d.png[/img]([i]Courtesy Birmingham Museums Trust's [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JZq9cBzrIVI]YouTube video[/url][/i])

All this research isn’t just for show—it actively influences how we design the game world. Here are a few ways historical accuracy is making its way into [i]God Save Birmingham[/i]:
[list]
[*][b]Landmarks & Architecture[/b] – We are recreating notable locations like St. Martin’s Church, Moor Hall, and the Marketplace, ensuring they are as close to their historical equivalents as possible.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45151109/a3320de70a4bf3109c80d61470e0436342bcda83.png[/img]
[*][b]Population Realism[/b] – The number of survivors (and zombies) in the game isn’t infinite—we’re basing it on the estimated 14th-century population of Birmingham. Every infected person you encounter was once part of that medieval town.
[*][b]Food & Animals[/b] – Within the game, you’ll only find food that would have actually been available in medieval Birmingham. That means bread, cheese, eggs, turnips, and more! You’ll also come across animals like chickens, which were commonly kept for their eggs and meat.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45151109/d38ea61eae78e4aa7069d36061eca783d14de80a.png[/img]
[*][b]Everyday Items[/b] – From bedding and tables to tools and cookware, we’ve researched the everyday objects people used in 14th-century Birmingham to make the world feel authentic. You’ll also find historically accurate lighting sources, like rushlights, an inexpensive type of lamp made from animal fat and reeds.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45151109/447a58bfc4e4821e3601eadc25fc0ef139e7cf45.jpg[/img][/list]
We’re committed to making this world feel as realistic as possible, but we know there’s always more to learn. If you have any knowledge of medieval Birmingham—whether it’s historical sources, family research, or just cool facts—please share it with us within our [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/3073940/discussions/0/604147304925038120/]Steam discussion board[/url]! Your input could help shape the game even further.

Let us know your thoughts, and stay tuned for more updates!

Thank you,
[i]God Save Birmingham[/i] Team

notes.title: Introducing God Save Birmingham and 2025 Plans
notes.notes:
Hello, I’m Hyeonseong Cha, a programmer and Creative Director of [i]God Save Birmingham[/i].

We’ve been working hard on [i]God Save Birmingham[/i] since we first introduced the game last year. Today we’d like to tell you a little more about it and share our plans for 2025.

A short description of [i]God Save Birmingham[/i] would be, “a zombie apocalypse survival game in a medieval European town”. When I first played survival games like [i]Don’t Starve[/i] or [i]Project Zomboid[/i], I found it difficult to survive even a single day, and the experience of overcoming such a difficult environment was very memorable and satisfying. My hope is that we can create a game like that, and bring a similar experience to fans of the genre. So when you step into the world of [i]God Save Birmingham[/i], you’ll find yourself in a truly desperate and challenging scenario.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45151109/4ecfabb1ed6b4123cf0506243a6acebda9c6a902.gif[/img]
[i][One of game’s unique characteristics is an aim-based strike system.][/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45151109/57c0688c1a9455895e5216ff16452783976342b9.gif[/img]
[i][Battles with zombies are intense, but the other survival activities won’t be any easier.][/i]

Zombie apocalypse settings are one of my favorites across any media. But while there are a lot of different games that feature zombies, they’re not often that classic slow-walking kind that I like most. The terror they create as the horde closes in… the tension as a crowd of them grabs hold and goes in for the bite… These are the thrills I love most about the genre. It’s tricky to capture that type of enemy and bring them to life in a game, but we’re embracing that challenge head-on.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45151109/37c2652f88b8caf832814830fda6062d37b6fb1c.gif[/img]
[i][Another unique feature: our zombies’ procedural grappling system.][/i]

One of our goals from the beginning was to recreate an entire town in a virtual space, and build apocalyptic survival gameplay around it. We’ve put a huge amount of time and care into achieving the right historical feeling and geographic scope. Sometimes that’s meant compromising on our loftier ambitions (as we’re a pretty small team), but we’re confident in our ability to deliver a setting with the kind of depth and size players have come to expect.

We ultimately chose to recreate a medium-sized city in medieval Europe and researched a bunch of them. In the end, Birmingham in the 1300s fit the criteria we were looking for.

You may have seen Birmingham or other communities like it in other media with a more fantastical tone. But what we’re trying to present is something that reflects a grounded, realistic picture of day-to-day life in that time and place. In our research, we’ve strived to be as faithful as possible to the location and appearance of the various churches, manors, village centers, and other infrastructure that existed in Birmingham in real-life history.

We’re also working to recreate the typical household items, food, and tools of the time accurately (or as close as we can get within reason), to really convey the textured feeling of what it would be like to try to survive a disaster scenario back then.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45151109/9610283ed0859c523016afd25d65306ce6a08121.png[/img][i][A bed of straw offers a comfortable place to rest.][/i]

We’ll be releasing a video soon to share what we’ve been working on, and we’re planning to showcase the game through game shows or other channels so people can have a chance to experience it for themselves. We believe there are a lot of people out there who are both fans of zombie fiction and nerds for medieval history, like we are. And while the game is still in a pretty early stage, we’re really looking forward to the day when players can get their hands on it, explore the world we’ve built, and share feedback that can make [i]God Save Birmingham[/i] even better.

I’m happy to finally share a bit of our thoughts and plans for the game, and we’re working on some other ideas for how we can keep players up to date with the game’s development. We still have a lot to share with you, so we’ll be back soon!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45151109/7be581bf978676751a76388b97ca69311581b870.jpg[/img]
[i][Cologne, Germany, during Gamescom 2024 – In the Cologne Cathedral, with a grateful heart.][/i]

Thank you,
Hyeonseong Cha, Creative Director

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45151109/24a55c80e0161e98833371a79e2691971985e25c.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45151109/f034df749a3d7678d7eb1c5077a0790a82eaa154.jpg[/img][i][Here you see Hyeonseong Cha, God Save Birmingham's director][/i]

notes.title: Here's an open world zombie survival game set in medieval.... Birmingham?
notes.notes:
I can guarantee you that a zombie survival game called God Save Birmingham wasn't on your "2024 Video Game Announcements" bingo card. It takes place in 14th century England, and tasks you with fending off the rampant zombie hordes of a populace who've succumbed to a mysterious case of reanimation. Perhaps the cause is that there's no Maccies or TK Maxx at the local Bull Ring yet.

notes.title: Welcome to God Save Birmingham
notes.notes:
Dear Survivor,

Welcome to the first day of the rest of your life in God Save Birmingham.

Thank you for finding our humble abode on Steam and joining us on our path to create a hardcore zombie survival sandbox set in medieval Birmingham, with real physics and beautiful graphics set in medieval Birmingham.

We've been working on the game for only five months so far–with just two of us in the first four months, and now a strong team of six. With a bigger team, we hope to ramp up our development to bring you the playable version of God Save Birmingham as soon as possible.

Our studio’s belief is that our game can stand out as one of the best in the genre by listening to and integrating feedback from our players, who also love the genre as we do. Rest assured that we always hold fast to this belief and plan to bring you betas to test, and then launch into Early Access to polish the game with you over multiple updates.

We can't wait to share what we're working on as we go, so WISHLIST and FOLLOW us to stay informed of new waves of the infestation.

May God Save Birmingham,
ODS Team

notes.title: Hear Ye, Hear Ye We Have An Announcement
notes.notes:
Well met!

We are pleased to announce that our newest title, [b]God Save Birmingham[/b], will be attending [b]Gamescom [/b]([b]Booth: C079[/b] located in [b]Hall: 10.1[/b]), and [b]PAX West[/b] ([b]Booth: 317[/b]) this year. We are excited to share this momentous experience as we reveal our latest title to the world.

[b]God Save Birmingham[/b] immerses you in a struggle for survival set in 14th-century Birmingham, England. While you may think staying alive is just about scavenging for food and water, you would be wrong. This challenging zombie survival game is filled with physics-based mechanics, which both help and hamper your efforts to survive the undead. Move, lift, and barricade using objects to help prolong your survival. Watch your step as you run from your former neighbors, or you might find yourself tripping as gravity is not your friend. Stab, kick, and stomp your way through Birmingham; perhaps you will prevail in this forsaken town.

Still seems easy ay? Swing by our booths to give it a try and we’ll see if you can escape the horrors of Birmingham. If you have any questions, feel free to catch any one of our ODS Team members lurking around the booth! 

[h3][b]Here’s what our booth will look like at Gamescom![/b][/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45151109/92eeb13e9180868d84e9e9f7e0240fffcced9da3.png[/img]

Can’t wait to meet you all!

Kind regards,
-ODS Team
